Surface ownership in the more than 1.1 million acres in the Ceded Area include, approximately 9,000 acres of tribal land; 17,000 acres of allotted land; 45,000 acres of state land; and over 1,000,000 acres of private fee land.
Lease Terms
In late 1970, the Crow Tribe, after consultation with the BIA and USGS, sought bids for Mineral Prospecting Permits. By assignment from the competitive high bidder, Westmoreland Resources received permits on two of the tracts offered in the Crow Ceded Area. Tract No. 3., Sale 3. was on 14,745.92 acres and Tract 2., Sale 3. was on 16,130.33 acres. Consideration for the two prospecting permits totaled $459,476.48 and gave Westmoreland Resources an exclusive right for two years to prospect for coal in the permit acreage. The permits provided options to lease and Westmoreland Resources exercised their option in June, 1972. Royalty under the June, 1972 leases was 17 1/2c per ton of coal during the first ten years; the royalty rate was to be renegotiable at ten year intervals so long as coal was produced in paying quantities. In addition to royalty an annual rental of $1.00 per acre was included.
